title: Paperback: The Game
provenance: Reported not launching by udance4ever (highball-db#349, 2026-10-06), Apple M1, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.9, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r21, every graphics mode. Reproduced here on an M4 (macOS 27.0, r21, 2026-10-06), both the 32-bit Paperback.exe that Steam starts and the 64-bit Paperback64.exe beside it.
notes: Plays on the Wine 11 engine r21 or later, which Play offers by itself since Highball 0.10.12. The game is built on the Loom engine (SDL and OpenGL, 2017), so the graphics mode setting does not apply to it. On older engines it crashed a second after start, because macOS's old-style OpenGL 2.1 context lacks a function the game loads (glClearDepthf), and engine patch 0021 in r21 answers it. The game also mixes its music louder than full scale. Windows' audio engine turns such peaks down before the speakers, while Wine on a Mac clipped them, which made loud parts sound like a bad bitrate. The Wine 11 engines r22 and r23 (Highball 0.10.15) add a limiter that does what Windows does. On r23 the reporter still hears the music as too loud (highball-db#349), not yet compared with Windows.

knownIssues.symptom: Wine's Program Error dialog (winedbg) right at launch, page fault on read access at address 0, on every graphics mode
knownIssues.cause: the game calls glClearDepthf, which Wine's opengl32 withholds in macOS's OpenGL 2.1 context (needs GL_ARB_ES2_compatibility or OpenGL 4.1); measured with WINEDEBUG=warn+opengl,+wgl on an M4
knownIssues.fix: engine x64-crossover26.3-r21 (Wine 11, patch 0021), shipped in Highball 0.10.11; reaches the title menu on an M4; confirmed by the reporter on an M1 (highball-db#349). Highball 0.10.12 and later offer r21 on Play

knownIssues.symptom: Loud parts of the music sound harsh, like a bad bitrate
knownIssues.cause: The game mixes its music above full scale (the title music goes over in 25 of every 30 seconds, measured on an M4). Windows' audio engine limits such peaks, and Wine on a Mac clipped them
knownIssues.fix: The Wine 11 engine r23, or r22 for D3DMetal 4, carries Highball's limiter from Highball 0.10.15. Pick it on the environment's Full page under Advanced, Engine. On r23 the reporter still hears the music as too loud (highball-db#349), not compared with Windows yet
